entry.title: [UPDATED] GHSA-rhgq-f8x5-j2jc: Keycloak's identity-first login flow exposes user information
entry.content:
Keycloak's identity-first login flow exposes user information

Aliases: CVE-2026-4633

Severity: CVSS_V3: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:L/I:N/A:N

Affected:

  • org.keycloak:keycloak-services — fixed in 26.6.1
  • org.keycloak:keycloak-services — fixed in 26.4.12

A flaw was found in Keycloak. A remote attacker can exploit differential error messages during the identity-first login flow when Organizations are enabled. This vulnerability allows an attacker to determine the existence of users, leading to information disclosure through user enumeration.

entry.title: [UPDATED] GHSA-v897-pv23-r8cw: Keycloak has an improper input validation vulnerability
entry.content:
Keycloak has an improper input validation vulnerability

Aliases: CVE-2026-0976

Severity: CVSS_V3: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:L/I:N/A:N

Affected:

  • org.keycloak:keycloak-quarkus-server

A flaw was found in Keycloak. This improper input validation vulnerability occurs because Keycloak accepts RFC-compliant matrix parameters in URL path segments, while common reverse proxy configurations may ignore or mishandle them. A remote attacker can craft requests to mask path segments, potentially bypassing proxy-level path filtering. This could expose administrative or sensitive endpoints that operators believe are not externally reachable.

entry.title: [UPDATED] GHSA-m32f-8vh9-2hh3: Keycloak: Arbitrary code execution via Stored Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) in organization selection login page
entry.content:
Keycloak: Arbitrary code execution via Stored Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) in organization selection login page

Aliases: CVE-2026-37980

Severity: CVSS_V3: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:H/UI:R/S:C/C:H/I:L/A:N

Affected:

  • org.keycloak:keycloak-services

A flaw was found in Keycloak, specifically in the organization selection login page. A remote attacker with `manage-realm` or `manage-organizations` administrative privileges can exploit a Stored Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) vulnerability. This flaw occurs because the `organization.alias` is placed into an inline JavaScript `onclick` handler, allowing a crafted JavaScript payload to execute in a user's browser when they view the login page. Successful exploitation enables arbitrary JavaScript execution, potentially leading to session theft, unauthorized account actions, or further attacks against users of the affected realm.

entry.title: [UPDATED] GHSA-4pgc-gfrr-wcmg: Keycloak has Improper Access Control that allows attackers with valid credentials to bypass the allowRemoteResourceManagement=false
entry.content:
Keycloak has Improper Access Control that allows attackers with valid credentials to bypass the allowRemoteResourceManagement=false

Aliases: CVE-2026-4628

Severity: CVSS_V3: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:L/A:N

Affected:

  • org.keycloak:keycloak-services

A flaw was found in Keycloak. An improper Access Control vulnerability in Keycloak’s User-Managed Access (UMA) resource_set endpoint allows attackers with valid credentials to bypass the allowRemoteResourceManagement=false restriction. This occurs due to incomplete enforcement of access control checks on PUT operations to the resource_set endpoint. This issue enables unauthorized modification of protected resources, impacting data integrity.

entry.title: [NEW] GHSA-crwc-vw2r-qr6m: OGNL stricter-invocation block list bypass via java.lang.reflect reflection proxies
entry.content:
OGNL stricter-invocation block list bypass via java.lang.reflect reflection proxies

Aliases: CVE-2026-113730

Severity: CVSS_V3: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:L/I:L/A:L

Affected:

  • ognl:ognl — fixed in 3.4.13

### Summary OGNL's optional *stricter invocation* mode maintains a block list that prevents expressions from directly calling methods on dangerous classes such as `Runtime`, `ProcessBuilder`, and `ClassLoader`. The block list filters on the **declaring class of the method OGNL invokes**. Because `java.lang.reflect.Method` (and `Constructor`/`Field`) are not on the list, an expression can use reflection as a proxy — `someMethod.invoke(target, args)` — to reach a blocked method. The real call (e.g. `ProcessBuilder.start()`) then executes inside the JDK reflection machinery and never passes back through OGNL's `invokeMethod`, so the block list never sees it. ### Proof of concept Under the default OGNL context (public-only access, stricter invocation enabled), the following expression creat…

entry.title: [UPDATED] GHSA-rxjv-24xq-76wc: JavaCV: Integer Overflow in IPCameraFrameGrabber Causes Infinite-Loop DoS
entry.content:
JavaCV: Integer Overflow in IPCameraFrameGrabber Causes Infinite-Loop DoS

Aliases: CVE-2026-102834

Severity: CVSS_V3: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H

Affected:

  • org.bytedeco:javacv — fixed in 1.5.14

### Summary `IPCameraFrameGrabber` parses the `Content-Length` value from the multipart MJPEG HTTP stream returned by the configured IP camera without any bounds checking. A malicious or compromised camera endpoint - or any network attacker able to tamper with the plaintext HTTP response (these streams are conventionally accessed over `http://`, as documented in the class itself) - can supply a `Content-Length` value in the range `1073741825`-`2147483647`. This drives the internal buffer-growth routine `ensureBufferCapacity(int)` into 32-bit signed integer overflow, which turns the "grow the buffer" loop into a true infinite loop: the loop variable oscillates to `0` and never again satisfies the loop's exit condition. The thread that called `grab()`/`grabBufferedImage()` spins at 100% CPU …

entry.title: [UPDATED] GHSA-h9h9-2rmf-rvhp: Junrar: RarVM VM_JMP maxOpCount bypass causes infinite CPU loop during RAR4 extraction
entry.content:
Junrar: RarVM VM_JMP maxOpCount bypass causes infinite CPU loop during RAR4 extraction

Aliases: CVE-2026-97370

Severity: CVSS_V3: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H

Affected:

  • com.github.junrar:junrar — fixed in 7.6.1

### Summary Junrar's RAR virtual machine can be forced into a deterministic infinite loop while extracting a crafted RAR4 archive. The `RarVM.ExecuteCode` loop is intended to be bounded by `maxOpCount`, but jump instructions can bypass this limit when `setIP()` is called with a target instruction pointer greater than or equal to `codeSize`. An unauthenticated attacker who can provide a RAR archive to an application using `Junrar.extract()` can cause the extraction thread to spin forever, consuming CPU and blocking the process. The issue is a denial of service vulnerability, not remote code execution. ### Details The root cause is in `src/main/java/com/github/junrar/unpack/vm/RarVM.java`. `setIP()` returns early when the target IP is outside the prepared VM program: ```java private bo…
